name: Jack Reed
stance: Calls for congressional oversight, standards and speed limits on AI, including military AI use, criticizes rejection of AI guardrails and chip sales to China, and opposes preempting states' ability to regulate AI.

statements.text: Original cosponsor, with Sens. Romney, Moran, King and Hassan, of the Preserving American Dominance in Artificial Intelligence Act of 2024 (S. 5616), which would establish an Artificial Intelligence Safety Review Office in the Department of Commerce to oversee covered frontier AI models.
There should be no deal that gives Big Tech free rein & takes away states’ rights & ability to protect their citizens.
We have to allow states to take the lead because we’re not able to, so far in Washington, come up with appropriate legislation
More bipartisan evidence showing Trump’s U-Turn on advanced AI chip sales to China is a colossal economic and national security failure.

Introduced with Sen. Coons the Responsible Artificial Intelligence Defense (RAIDA) Act, which would require human operators to be able to monitor and manually deactivate AI-enabled autonomous systems, bar AI from nuclear decision-making, and require testing before fielding.
To begin, we should formalize international norms for military and civilian uses of AI to regulate areas where full human control over the technology is essential.
His shortsighted view increases the likelihood that AI will be misused by bad actors or unsafely sped up by corporate interests at the expense of the public.
Congress must play a role in establishing clear guardrails & sensible speed limits for AI use by our armed forces.
With Sens. Warner and Coons, demanded immediate investigations into reports of dangers from rushed AI deployment by the U.S. military.
